title: Space Is Closer Than You Think
premise: The official boundary of space — the Kármán line — is only 100 km up, a scale almost nobody feels intuitively. Laddering up through the atmosphere makes that number visceral.
target_audience: Curious general audience, science/tech Shorts viewers, 9:16 vertical
hook: Space is closer than you think — just one hundred kilometers straight up. You could drive there in an hour.
emotional_purpose: Awe through scale; reframe 'space' as near, not far
curiosity_mechanism: Number shock + escalating altitude ladder; each beat reveals a higher, stranger landmark
payoff: Space isn't far away. It's right above the clouds — the doorway is just very, very high.

beats.label: Hook — 100 km
beats.narration: Space is closer than you think — just one hundred kilometers straight up. You could drive there in an hour.
beats.why_continue: Number shock + absurd comparison (drivable distance) demands justification

beats.label: The Kármán line
beats.narration: It's called the Kármán line — the altitude where the air gets too thin for wings to matter.
beats.why_continue: Names the mystery; origin story of the boundary

beats.label: Scale — the jet
beats.narration: Because here's the thing: a passenger jet cruises at ten kilometers. From the edge of space, that's a rounding error.

beats.label: The sky misbehaves
beats.narration: Keep climbing and the sky stops behaving. Meteors burn out around eighty kilometers. Auroras ripple a hundred and fifty up.
beats.why_continue: Visual spectacle + two new altitude landmarks

beats.label: Astronauts barely made it
beats.narration: And the International Space Station? Four hundred kilometers. Astronauts float there — but they're barely past the doorway, still skimming the top of the atmosphere.
beats.why_continue: Reframe of a famous fact; 'barely past the doorway' twist

beats.label: Payoff
beats.narration: Space isn't far away. It's right above the clouds — the doorway is just very, very high.
beats.why_continue: Payoff line + end card; loopable closer

factual_claims.claim: The FAI recognizes 100 km above sea level as the boundary of space (Kármán line).
Passenger jets cruise around 10–12 km (~35,000–40,000 ft).
Meteors become visible ~75–120 km and mostly disintegrate below ~95 km.
Green auroras typically occur 100–150 km up; during strong storms activity can extend beyond 300 km.
factual_claims.source: NOAA SWPC (spaceweather.gov aurora tutorial); UCAR SciEd; DLR

factual_claims.claim: The ISS orbits at roughly 400 km altitude.
The Kármán line marks roughly the altitude where the air is too thin for aerodynamic lift to sustain flight at orbital speeds.

style_note: No generic intro. Hook lands within 2 seconds. Numbers are the stars — typography carries them.
